file: File:Goddess Bau from Ur, c. 1800 BCE. Iraq Museum.jpg
description: Statue of a seated goddess, Bau (Nintinugga), from the Ningal Complex (Giparu, also called E-gig-par, or gig-par-ku) at the city of Ur, Iraq. Isin-Larsa period, c. 1800 BCE. Black diorite. Bau was the consort of the god Ninurta and the goddess of healing. On display the Iraq Museum in Baghdad, Iraq. U 6779B, IM 18663. Ur's 4th season of excavation by Sir Woolley, 1925-1926.

file: File:Mesopotamian female deity seating on a chair, Old-Babylonian fired clay plaque from Ur, Iraq.jpg
description: Mesopotamian female deity wearing a horned headdress and seating on a chair or a throne, probably Ishtar or Bau. The lunar symbol of the moon god Sin appears at the upper part, flanking the headdress. Elaborate dress and braided hair strands. Old-Babylonian period, 2003-1595 BCE. Fired clay plaque from Ur, Southern Mesopotamia, Iraq. The Sulaymaniyah Museum, Iraq.
